implementation_notes: C is where the seam is most often absent, because the vendor ships a header and the cheapest integration is `#include`ing it. The detection is the include graph plus the linker map: which vendor symbols does the binary actually reference, and which of them are called from domain code rather than from one adapter file. Consolidation is to isolate every vendor header behind one adapter per vendor API, expose your own header instead, and compile the adapter out when a replacement is selected. Vendor-defined structs in your own public headers are the worst case, because they make the vendor part of your ABI.
idiom_name: direct vendor SDK headers; vendor-defined structs in the domain
pitfalls: `vendor/cloud.h` included in a shared header propagates the vendor's types into every translation unit and into your ABI.
Link-time symbol visibility means the vendor dependency is discoverable with `nm`, which makes this the cheapest lock-in audit of any language here.
Vendor error codes mapped into your own enum is already a seam — and easy to leave incomplete, which is how a migration finds three unmapped codes at the end.
